discussion_comments.comment_body: Remote choice here is `branch.<b>.remote || origin`. `selectPrimaryGitRemoteUrl` in the workspace manifest uses `origin`, then the first remote. Two rules mean the manifest can show a different repo than the one this pushes to. Please unify them.

The selection rules remain different: handoff uses the current branch's remote, falling back to `origin`; manifest discovery has its own primary-remote preference. I have not marked this as unified. The confirmation displays the handoff plan's repository and remote, and both publication and cloud creation use that same plan, so the manifest cannot silently redirect this launch. Keeping the current selection in this PR avoids changing which repository existing branch configuration targets.

Core already wraps these in GitCommand and createWorkspaceGitReader ([[workspace-manifest.ts](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/789f79e46d3ba579717e8dc8be35fe28af935b06/sdk/packages/core/src/services/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts#L11-L54)](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/789f79e46d3ba579717e8dc8be35fe28af935b06/sdk/packages/core/src/services/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts#L11-L54)), and preflightCloudHandoffGit uses them. So the repo gets read twice with different rules: core only accepts a github.com upstream, while the sidecar has its own remote checks. The extra checks should move into core's preflight. Only the branch, commit, and push step should stay in the host.

🟢 **bug** (low)

The value sent in the `X-Task-ID` request header changed from the task ID to the ulid while the header name (and therefore the contract the Cline backend sees) stayed the same. If the backend treats this header as a task identifier (attribution, rate limiting, server-side joins), the meaning of the header silently changed; for tasks that have no ulid the header is also now empty where it previously always carried a value. This is probably intended as part of "ulid everywhere", but the header name no longer describes its content.

**建议**: Confirm with the backend owner which identifier this header is expected to carry, then either keep sending the task ID or rename the header (e.g. `X-Task-ULID`) so the contract stays unambiguous. If both ids are needed, send them as separate headers.

**证据**: `"X-Task-ID": this.options.ulid || "",`
